Move-Out Cleaning in Dallas: What Landlords and Property Managers Actually Check

Landlords don't just glance at the floors. Here's what Dallas property managers look at during a move-out walkthrough, and how to get every spot ready.

Get My Instant QuoteCall (469) 210-8005

Published 2026-10-20 · Salt of the Earth Cleaning Co.

Moving out is busy enough without worrying about the final walkthrough. Between packing, scheduling movers and setting up utilities at the new place, cleaning the old one often gets squeezed into the last few hours. That's usually when the details slip.

The good news: landlords and property managers in Dallas tend to check the same places. If you know where they look, you can focus your time where it counts. Here's what typically gets a closer look, and how to get each spot ready.

Start with your lease

Before you pick up a sponge, reread your lease and any move-out instructions from your property manager. Some ask for specific items, like cleaning inside the oven, wiping out the refrigerator, or replacing air filters and light bulbs. Others include a move-out checklist. Following their list is the simplest way to avoid surprises.

It also helps to find the photos or move-in report from when you arrived. Your goal is to leave the place as clean as you found it, allowing for normal wear.

The kitchen gets the most attention

If a landlord spends extra time anywhere, it's usually the kitchen.

Oven and stovetop

This is one of the first places people look. Clean inside the oven, including the racks and the glass door. Degrease the stovetop, drip pans or burner grates, the knobs and the outside of the range hood.

Refrigerator

Empty it completely, then wipe down every shelf and drawer. Clean the door seals, where crumbs and spills hide. Wipe the outside, including the top.

Cabinets and drawers

Empty every cabinet and drawer and wipe the inside, top to bottom. Don't forget shelf edges and handles. Crumbs left in a drawer are an easy thing for a manager to note.

Sink, counters and backsplash

Scrub the sink and polish the faucet. Wipe the counters and backsplash and clean the grout lines behind the faucet.

Bathrooms

Bathrooms show build-up quickly, and Dallas water can leave mineral spots behind.

  • Remove soap scum and hard water spots from the tub, shower walls and glass doors
  • Scrub tile and grout
  • Clean the toilet inside, outside, behind and around the base
  • Empty and wipe the vanity cabinet and drawers
  • Polish mirrors, faucets and fixtures
  • Clean the exhaust fan cover if it's dusty

The details people forget

These are the spots tenants often miss, and the ones a careful walkthrough catches:

  • Baseboards. Dust and scuffs collect along every wall. Hand-wipe them room by room.
  • Light switches and outlet covers. Fingerprints add up over a lease.
  • Doors and door frames. Wipe the fronts, edges and the tops of the frames.
  • Window sills and tracks. Vacuum out the dust and pollen, then wipe them down.
  • Ceiling fans and light fixtures. Dust the blades and clear out any bugs in the fixtures.
  • Closets. Wipe the shelves and vacuum the floor, including corners.
  • Blinds. Dust them slat by slat.
  • Floors. Vacuum carpets thoroughly and mop hard floors, especially along the edges.

Tips for an easier walkthrough

Clean after the movers leave. An empty home lets you reach every cabinet, closet and baseboard, and you won't have boxes in the way.

Leave a buffer. Schedule your clean a day or two before the walkthrough so there's time to handle anything that comes up.

Keep the utilities on. Cleaning needs running water and power, so wait to shut them off until the clean is done.

Take photos. Once everything is clean, walk through and photograph each room, the inside of the appliances and the bathrooms. It's a simple record for your own files.

Book early near month-end. Moving days cluster at the end of the month, so the best dates fill up first.

For property managers and landlords

If you're the one doing the walkthrough, a consistent turnover clean makes the next tenant's first impression easier to manage. A clean that covers inside the appliances, inside the cabinets and every baseboard means your next showing starts on the right foot.
